mainText: This is Dose of Good for Thursday, November 26. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Skin cancer treatment developed at a Brazilian university approved for public health system. The photodynamic therapy developed at the University of São Paulo's physics institute in São Carlos has been regulated for use in Brazil's public health system. According to the researchers, the method eliminates about 95% of treated tumours. Second: Firefighters rescue 66-year-old man from a 15-metre well in Brazil. A 66-year-old man fell into a dry well in rural Camocim, Ceará. Firefighters rigged a pulley system with a tripod and cables and brought him out conscious, with minor injuries and no complications. Third: Physicists trap a single positron for months. Northwestern University researchers captured a single particle of antimatter, a positron, cooled it close to absolute zero and held it in a trap for months. The feat will allow highly precise comparisons between antimatter and ordinary matter. Fourth: EU court orders a timeline for banning cages on farms. The EU Court of Justice ruled that the European Commission must set a new timeline for legislation ending cages for farm animals. The case came from a citizens' initiative with nearly 1.4 million signatures; about 300 million animals are still caged in the bloc. Fifth: Smart dental floss measures glucose and gum inflammation. Hong Kong researchers created a floss that collects a tiny drop of gum fluid in about 20 seconds and measures glucose, uric acid and other markers within minutes. Results closely matched blood tests. The device is still at the research stage. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
